root_cause.text: The BPF verifier’s helper prototype metadata in `bpf_func_proto` was missing or incorrect `MEM_RDONLY`/`MEM_WRITE` flags for several `ARG_PTR_TO_MEM` arguments, so after the verifier refactor it misclassified helper buffers as unchanged across calls and could wrongly optimize away later memory reads; in one case (`bpf_get_stack_proto_raw_tp`) the prototype even marked a write buffer as `MEM_RDONLY` instead of `ARG_PTR_TO_UNINIT_MEM`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly says “the verifier started relying on the access type flags in helper function prototypes” and that “several helper functions utilizing ARG_PTR_TO_MEM lack the corresponding MEM_RDONLY or MEM_WRITE flags,” causing the verifier to “incorrectly assume that the buffer contents are unchanged across the helper call”; the diff then adds `MEM_WRITE`/`MEM_RDONLY` to prototypes like `bpf_snprintf_proto`, `bpf_xdp_fib_lookup_proto`, `bpf_skb_fib_lookup_proto`, and changes `bpf_get_stack_proto_raw_tp` from `ARG_PTR_TO_MEM | MEM_RDONLY` to `ARG_PTR_TO_UNINIT_MEM`.

This group does not address that broader verifier prototype metadata bug or the specific helper involved.

This is the same class of verifier metadata bug that could affect helper buffer handling after the refactor.

The change directly fixes one of the root-cause prototype metadata errors: `bpf_get_stack_proto_raw_tp` was incorrectly marked as `MEM_RDONLY` instead of accepting `ARG_PTR_TO_UNINIT_MEM`, which matches the described verifier misclassification issue.

The change only marks IPv6 syncookie helper inputs as read-only, which is unrelated to the specific verifier metadata bug involving missing/incorrect MEM_RDONLY/MEM_WRITE flags on ARG_PTR_TO_MEM helpers and the bpf_get_stack_proto_raw_tp prototype.

candidates.rationale: This prototype marks the destination buffer argument as MEM_RDONLY even though the helper writes into it. That incorrect read-only classification is the root cause of the verifier misoptimizing helper buffer accesses after the refactor.

The output buffer argument is incorrectly tagged as MEM_RDONLY despite being written by bpf_snprintf_btf, which can cause the verifier to treat the buffer as unchanged and skip needed memory-read/update handling.

This is the destination buffer argument for bpf_read_branch_records, but it lacks writable-memory qualification. Without MEM_WRITE, the verifier may assume the helper does not modify the buffer and incorrectly optimize subsequent reads.
The bpf_xdp_fib_lookup output buffer is declared only as ARG_PTR_TO_MEM with no writable-memory flag, so the verifier can misclassify writes to the caller-provided buffer as having no effect.

This is the explicit bad prototype for bpf_get_stack_proto_raw_tp: it marks the stack output buffer as MEM_RDONLY instead of the required uninitialized/writeable buffer type, directly matching the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This prototype marks the stack output buffer as read-only memory, but the helper writes stack data into it. That incorrect MEM_RDONLY classification directly matches the root cause and can make the verifier treat the buffer as unchanged across calls.

The destination buffer for bpf_snprintf is written by the helper, yet it is tagged MEM_RDONLY here. This mislabels writable memory as read-only and can lead the verifier to misoptimize helper buffer accesses.
This output buffer argument for bpf_snprintf_btf is incorrectly marked MEM_RDONLY even though the helper writes into it. That is the same verifier metadata bug described in the root cause.
The bpf_xdp_fib_lookup destination buffer is missing writable-memory qualification. Without MEM_WRITE or equivalent, the verifier can wrongly assume helper writes do not change memory state.

This destination buffer argument for bpf_read_branch_records lacks writable-memory qualification. That omission can cause the verifier to treat the helper as not modifying the buffer, enabling incorrect read-elimination behavior.
